faq.question: How is the industry site different from the landing page?
faq.answer: The landing page is a custom design built in 14 days. The industry site is our ready-made demo tailored to your business, so it is faster and costs less.

faq.question: My industry is not on the list. What now?
faq.answer: Then the landing page or the business website is a better fit. Take the quote quiz and we will suggest the right plan from your answers.

faq.question: How many days does the industry site take?
faq.answer: 7 days, and we fix the deadline in the contract.

faq.question: Can I add features later?
faq.answer: Yes, as options from the price list: online payments, reviews, messengers, a second language, CRM. Option prices are on this page.

process.title: Brief and materials
process.text: Before day one: a short written brief with the CAD file if you have one, or photos and drawings if there is no model; if you need it, we sign an NDA before you send the file. In reply you get the estimate, the deadline, the start date and a draft contract, all before any payment. Then a 50% prepayment, a detailed brief with photos and videos of the parts, and your materials; our questions about the parts come as one list. Day one is the start date if the detailed brief and materials are in by then, otherwise the day they arrive.

process.title: Geometry and angles
process.text: We sign off the model, the camera angles and the parts the scene explains with you. The scene is built after the sign-off.

process.title: Scene and parts
process.text: We build the scene, a camera move to every part, labels and the inquiry form inside the scene. For a 3D block this step is week 2.

process.title: Poster, phones, audit
process.text: A poster frame for the first screen, a poster and a video for phones without WebGL 2.0, a preliminary Lighthouse audit. A 3D landing page also gets its page around the scene; for a 3D block this step is week 3.

process.title: Revisions and launch
process.text: Two rounds of revisions, a final Lighthouse audit for the acceptance certificate, launch, source code handover and a 30-day warranty. For a 3D block this step is week 4.

faq.question: We don't have a 3D model — what now?
faq.answer: We build one from scratch using photos and drawings. It is a separate line in both the estimate and the schedule, priced before any prepayment so the cost does not change mid-project.

faq.question: How does 3D work on older phones?
faq.answer: A poster frame shows first and the scene loads after it. Phones without WebGL 2.0 show a poster and a video instead of the scene, and the inquiry form works either way. On a slow phone the scene may rotate less smoothly, but the poster, labels and inquiry form are there right away.

faq.question: How much do extra revisions cost?
faq.answer: Two rounds of revisions are included: texts, colors, highlights. After that we bill at the hourly rate from the price list. A new part or camera angle after the geometry sign-off is estimated separately before any work starts.

faq.question: Can you put 3D on Tilda, WordPress or 1C-Bitrix?
faq.answer: No. Not Tilda, not WordPress, not 1C-Bitrix: we only work with code. A 3D block goes into a site built in code — yours if developers wrote it without a website builder, or one we built. We can build a whole 3D landing page on a subdomain, linked from your site.

faq.question: What is the difference between a 3D block and a 3D landing page?
faq.answer: A 3D block is one interactive scene embedded into a site built in code, yours or one we built. A 3D landing page is a single page around the scene: we write the copy from your brief, and the page carries the inquiry form and the whole site base, analytics included.

faq.question: Can someone download our model from the site?
faq.answer: Yes, like any image on a website. That is why the site gets a lightweight display copy: the outside look and the parts you approved for display, without the other internal details, tolerances or drawings. We never share the drawings or the source model with third parties.

meta.title: Privacy policy
meta.description: What data the MRSHKN studio website collects, why, where it goes and how to withdraw your consent.

operator.title: Who processes your data
paragraphs: The data controller is Veronika Viktorovna Murashkina, a self-employed professional in Russia trading as MRSHKN studio (taxpayer ID 421815967902).
For any question about your data, email hello@mrshkn.com.

data.title: What data we collect
paragraphs: From the request you send through the brief on this website:
items: your name;
how to reach you: phone, email or messenger handle;
your brief answers: what you need built, industry, style, timing, budget and comments;
campaign tags, if you came from an ad.

purposes.title: Why we process it
paragraphs: We use request data to reply to you, discuss your project and prepare a proposal.
We use analytics data to see website traffic and understand which pages and ads work.

basis.title: Legal basis
paragraphs: We process your data based on your consent. You consent to the processing of your request by ticking the box in the brief before sending it, and to analytics cookies by clicking “Accept” in the cookie banner.

transfer.title: Where your data goes
paragraphs: Your whole request — name, contact details, brief answers and campaign tags — is saved in the website's database. It can only be opened from the site's admin panel, after signing in with a login and password.

The name and contact details from your request, together with your brief answers, are sent to Telegram: the studio's bot posts a notification about each new request to the studio's group chat. The site's server reaches Telegram through Cloudflare, so these details pass through Cloudflare on their way to Telegram. Telegram and Cloudflare are services based outside Russia.
A copy of your request is emailed to hello@mrshkn.com, the studio mailbox hosted by Yandex.
Analytics data goes to Yandex (Yandex Metrica) and Google (Google Analytics 4), and only after you consent. Google is a service based outside Russia.

storage.title: Where and how long data is stored
paragraphs: The website and its database run on a Timeweb Cloud server in Novosibirsk, Russia.
We keep request data for as long as we need it to reply and work on your project. Email hello@mrshkn.com and we will delete it sooner.

cookies.title: Cookies and analytics
paragraphs: Yandex Metrica and Google Analytics 4 only start after you click “Accept” in the cookie banner. Until then your browser does not contact them, and after “Decline” they never load.
Without analytics, the website sets only its own cookies: your banner choice, the style and theme you picked and, if you came from an ad, campaign tags so they reach your request.
You can change your mind at any time: use the button below and the banner will appear again.

rights.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Email hello@mrshkn.com if you want to:
items: find out what data we hold about you;
correct or delete it;
withdraw your consent to the processing of your request.

mail.subject: {project}: three questions from Nikolay at MRSHKN
paragraphs: Hello,

This is Nikolay from MRSHKN. We built {project} together, and I would like to know how the work looks from your side. I will show your review on the studio's website — it will tell new clients more than anything I could say.

The form has three questions: what brought you to us, how the work went and what changed after launch. Answer as you like, short or long — I publish criticism too and only fix typos. It takes about ten minutes, no sign-up or passwords:
{link}
The form asks for your full name only for the consent — it will not appear on the site. The review is signed the way you choose, for example “Anna, coffee shop on Main Street”.
You can send the review only with consent to publish it — there are two checkboxes at the end of the form. If you change your mind, reply to this email and I will take it down.
The link works for 60 days. Thank you for the project.
Nikolay, MRSHKN studio
